title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: More Expensive, But Google Plan to Use It for Everything
description: At Google I/O, Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash without the '-preview' modifier, going straight to general availability. Google appears to be using it extensively across their key products, marking a significant shift in their AI deployment strategy.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Last Six Months in LLMs in Five Minutes - PyCon US 2026 Lightning Talk
description: Simon Willison delivered a lightning talk at PyCon US 2026 with annotated slides covering recent LLM developments. He used his custom presentation tool to create annotated slides, summarizing key trends in AI and LLMs from the past six months.
author: Simon Willison

title: How Claude Code Works in Large Codebases - Hacker News Discussion
description: A highly upvoted Hacker News discussion (241 points) about how Claude Code operates in large codebases, with community insights on AI-assisted programming workflows and best practices for working with AI coding tools at scale.
author: Hacker News Community

title: I Believe There Are Entire Companies Right Now Under AI Psychosis - Mitchell Hashimoto
description: Mitchell Hashimoto's tweet about 'AI psychosis' became the most upvoted story on Hacker News (1854 points), sparking intense discussion about the current state of AI adoption, hype cycles, and whether companies are making irrational decisions around AI technology.
author: Mitchell Hashimoto

title: OpenClaw's Naming History: From Warelay to Personal AI Assistant
description: Simon Willison traced the complete Git history of his OpenClaw project, revealing it went through six different names: Warelay → CLAWDIS → CLAWDBOT → Clawdbot → Moltbot → OpenClaw. The project evolved from a WhatsApp relay CLI to a personal AI assistant.
author: Simon Willison

title: Programming Languages Are Increasingly Fungible in the Era of Coding Agents
description: Simon Willison discussed how coding agents are making programming languages less about lock-in and more interchangeable. Citing Mitchell Hashimoto's comments on Bun porting from Zig to Rust: 'Programming languages used to be LOCK IN, and they're increasingly not so.' Willison shared a story about a company using coding agents to rewrite both iOS and Android apps to React Native.
author: Simon Willison / Mitchell Hashimoto

title: Welcome to the Datasette Blog - Built with OpenAI Codex Desktop
description: Simon Willison launched the official Datasette blog, built entirely using OpenAI Codex desktop. He highlighted that Codex now has the Markdown session transcript export feature he'd always wanted, making it easier to document AI-assisted development workflows.
author: Simon Willison

title: Show HN: Find the Best Local LLM for Your Hardware, Ranked by Benchmarks
description: A Hacker News submission (282 points) showcasing a tool to help users find the best local LLM for their specific hardware, with models ranked by benchmarks. This reflects the growing trend of running LLMs locally and the need for hardware-aware model selection.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Bun Rust Rewrite: Codebase Fails Basic Miri Checks, Allows for UB in Safe Rust
description: A Hacker News discussion (464 points) about Bun's Rust rewrite, with users pointing out that the codebase 'fails basic miri checks and allows for UB (undefined behavior) in safe Rust.' This sparked debate about the safety trade-offs in rapid development with AI assistance.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Three Types of Programmers in 2026 - Context Window Management as Key Skill
description: Andrej Karpathy discussed how the role of programmers is evolving in 2026, with context window management becoming a key skill. He emphasizes that 'what's in the context window is your lever over the interpreter, that is the LLM.' This highlights the shift from traditional coding to context engineering.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Software 3.0: Programming Paradigm Shift Around Prompts
description: Andrej Karpathy promoted the concept of 'Software 3.0' - a new programming layer built around prompts rather than traditional code. He explains this is not just another developer tool but a fundamental shift in how programming works, moving from code to prompts as the primary abstraction.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Vibe Coding is the Future - Amjad Masad on Moonshots Podcast
description: Amjad Masad discussed why 'vibe coding' is not just a trend but the future of programming, sharing insights on AI coding impact on engineering teams and the post-coding AI era. He emphasized that this approach represents a fundamental shift in how software will be built.
author: Amjad Masad

title: Replit Raises $400M Series D at $9B Valuation
description: Replit raised $400M in Series D funding with a $9B valuation, focusing on democratizing software creation with AI coding tools. The company has grown to 34M users with their AI coding platform, signaling strong investor confidence in AI-assisted development platforms.
author: Amjad Masad / Replit

title: Karpathy's Dramatic Shift in Coding Workflow: From 80% Manual to AI-First
description: Andrej Karpathy revealed a dramatic shift in his programming workflow 'in just a few weeks' due to improved LLM coding capabilities. He moved from '80% manual+autocomplete coding and 20% agents' to a much more AI-assisted approach, demonstrating how rapidly AI coding tools are evolving.
author: Jason Guo / Andrej Karpathy
